audit.whatIsWrong: Lane difficulty prose was generic; the decisive early gate is Gravity Field's uptime, not 'range'.
audit.why: Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1 down to 13s at rank 5 and is the only thing that stops Lunar Rush landing; the whole lane is fought around that timer.
audit.corrected: Difficulty stays 7/10 TRICKY but is now expressed as the Gravity Field timer in cooldowns, dosFull and the level chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed across layers: full-layer phases[0..5].side read Viktor/Viktor/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while content win[] read Diana/Diana/Viktor/Viktor/Diana/Diana; win[6] said Diana while both prose fields said Viktor scales past you.
audit.why: Content win[] matches the packet levelChart for rows 0-5, so full was the stale layer. For 2+ items both whys[6] and phases[6].side already said Viktor, so win[6] was the outlier.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 aligned to Diana/Diana/Viktor/Viktor/Diana/Diana; win[6] moved to Viktor. Every moved row's why rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated ability names 'Death Ray' and 'Chaos Storm'; the Siphon Power auto-reset tell was absent; no statement that a Moonlight mark refunds Lunar Rush.
audit.why: Riot's kit gives Hextech Ray (E, 12/11/10/9/8s) and Arcane Storm (R, 120/100/80s). Siphon Power empowers his next basic attack, so the wind-up is the burst tell. Lunar Rush has no cooldown onto a Moonlight target and is 22s at rank 1 otherwise.
audit.corrected: Real names used throughout; the reset rule and the auto-attack tell now appear in dosFull/dontsFull.

audit.why: It is the field that must carry real numbers.
audit.corrected: Gravity Field 17s/13s, Hextech Ray 12s, Arcane Storm 120s vs Moonfall 100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Bodies must explain their own titles.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with kit-grounded bodies matching their titles.

edits.before: E pull joins... no — your dash threat begins: Q-mark into E reset chases are live; trade on every landed crescent.
edits.after: Level 3 he has Gravity Field: 17s of stun zone drops on your landing spot, so trade only after he spends it.

edits.before: Mark-dash trades on cooldown — Q, E to the mark, passive three-hit, walk. The lane respects the curve now.
edits.after: His Hextech Ray hits 11s here and Gravity Field 17s — you get one mark-dash trade per stun zone, not a rotation.

edits.before: Late Diana dives: E the carry through the front line, R the clump that collapses, and reset through the wreckage.
edits.after: Two items in, his Arcane Storm and 8s Hextech Rays out-range you — you need a flank or a pick, not a straight fight.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Pale Cascade for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — the stun zone owns every all-in, so walk out the instant it drops and step up on its downtime. - Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1; his Arcane Storm is 120s, and your Moonfall answers at 100s.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Crescent Strike's 900 range beats his 600 Siphon Power — arc it over the wave onto him and the Moonlight mark makes your dash free.

edits.before: Q through the wave onto his chest, E the mark, three-hit string, walk — the phase trade he answers after you've left.
edits.after: Pale Cascade's orbs pop on contact and the third grows the shield — step in as they spawn so his Siphon Power auto hits shield.

edits.before: Viktor burns Gravity Field on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Q first, then E — a Moonlight target refunds Lunar Rush, so the dash is free.

edits.before: That’s Viktor’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Lunar Rush refunds only onto a Moonlight target — without one you burn 22s.

edits.before: Dashing onto an unmarked target with W down — Diana without the reset or the shield is a melee mage donating proximity.
edits.after: No Moonlight mark means Lunar Rush costs its full 22s at rank 1 and leaves you inside Gravity Field with no way back out.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Viktor wins by dropping Gravity Field on your landing spot, stunning you mid-dash, then farming you with 12s Hextech Rays.

edits.before: Carry through the dive — mark, dash, pull, delete; your R turns their teamfight spacing into a suggestion.
edits.after: Viktor stands behind his front line and steers Arcane Storm — Moonfall the collapse and delete him first.

edits.before: Death Ray poke and Gravity Field zoning fully counter your dash-in style once his augments are complete.
edits.after: Hextech Ray poke and Gravity Field zoning counter your dash-in style once his Hex Fragment augments are complete.

edits.before: His completed Hex Core kit and first item let his ranged poke out-damage anything you can do in an even trade.
edits.after: Your first item makes the mark-dash lethal — he cannot poke you down before you delete him on Gravity Field's downtime.

edits.before: Once he completes Hex Core upgrades and a first item, Chaos Storm plus Death Ray poke starts out-damaging your engage attempts and he can zone you off waves entirely.
edits.after: Once he completes Hex Core upgrades and a first item, Arcane Storm plus Hextech Ray poke starts out-damaging your engage attempts and he can zone you off waves entirely.

edits.before: Early Viktor is genuinely weak in lane: no shield, no real escape, and Death Ray poke damage is minimal before his Hex Core augments unlock. Your Q-E-Q all-in at level 3 punishes him hard, and you should be aggressively contesting every trade you can in this window. Deny his CS to delay his power spike as long as possible.
edits.after: Early Viktor is genuinely weak in lane: no escape, and Hextech Ray poke damage is minimal before his Hex Fragment augments unlock. Your Q-E-Q all-in at level 3 punishes him hard, and you should be contesting every trade you can while Gravity Field is down. Deny his CS to delay his power spike as long as possible.

edits.before: Once he completes his Hex Core 2 upgrade around mid-game, Viktor's Gravity Field zoning and Death Ray poke damage spike dramatically, letting him control the lane and punish your engages from range. This is the point where lane priority starts shifting to him, and pushing an all-in into a completed Gravity Field is a losing proposition. Your level 6 still gives you reach to punish overextensions, but you need to be more careful about when you commit.
edits.after: Once he completes his Hex Core 2 upgrade around mid-game, Viktor's Gravity Field zoning and Hextech Ray poke damage spike dramatically, letting him control the lane and punish your engages from range. This is the point where lane priority starts shifting to him, and pushing an all-in into a live Gravity Field is a losing proposition. Your level 6 still gives you reach to punish overextensions, but commit only once that 13-17s field is spent.

edits.before: Fully scaled Viktor with Chaos Storm and completed items is one of the strongest teamfight and poke mid-laners in the game, out-damaging you at range without ever entering your kill range. Your best play late is picking him off in side lanes or catching him out of position rather than walking into his AOE ult in a straight fight. Prioritize denying his farm earlier in the game so this scaling threat never fully materializes.
edits.after: Fully scaled Viktor with Arcane Storm and completed items is one of the strongest teamfight and poke mid-laners in the game, out-damaging you at range without ever entering your kill range. Your best play late is picking him off in side lanes or catching him out of position rather than walking into his 80s ult in a straight fight. Prioritize denying his farm earlier in the game so this scaling threat never fully materializes.
